text.p: Poco Petroleums Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to increase its capital spending in 1997 to C$500 million from the previously budgeted C$400 million.

Poco, which reported big increases in oil and gas reserves and production for the first half, said the richer budget would consist of C$400 million for exploration and development and C$100 million for acquisitions.

"This program was increased from C$400 million due to increased drilling projected for the fourth quarter, additional Crown (government) land acquisitions and the O'Chiese and Alder Flats plant expansions," the company said.

It said its 1997 production was expected to average 460 million cubic feet of natural gas and 40,000 barrels of oil and gas liquids a day. Exit rates for 1997 were projected at 500 million cubic feet of gas and 44,000 barrels of oil and liquids a day.

Poco said its 1997 cash flow was expected to reach C$2.50 to C$2.60 a share, based on assumptions of C$22 a barrel for oil and liquids (US$20 per barrel WTI) and C$1.90 per thousand cubic feet of gas.
The company's cash flow in 1996 was C$2.02 a share.
